name: Azaziah
overview: Azaziah was a male Levite who served as an overseer of the consecrated things under Conaniah. His role involved responsibility over sacred duties and items, indicating a position of trust within the Levitical priesthood. There are no additional notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Azaziah means 'y-h-v-h is strong,' reflecting a theophoric element that honors the strength of the Lord. This proper name situates him within the biblical tradition of names expressing faith in God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Azaziah as a descendant of Levi, linking him to the priestly tribe entrusted with temple service. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no further family relationships are recorded.
scriptureSignificance: Azaziah's significance lies in his administrative role within the Levitical system, specifically overseeing consecrated items under Conaniah's authority. This highlights the organized and reverent care given to sacred responsibilities in Israel's worship, demonstrating faithfulness to God's commands in temple service.
